draft_context.source_title: ‘The next major music platform should give people something to do with the music’: Spotify’s former Head of Innovation on his plans to launch an interactive music service, and whether AI features will help or hinder streaming
draft_context.description: The current state of music streaming is interesting, yet unpredictable. The shift from the CD era into the streaming era has made access to music more ubiquitous, but it’s also thrown up problems: some users aren’t interacting with music like they did before, and the explosive spread of AI is threatening the entire streaming model. Enter Mauhan M. Zonoozy, former Head of Innovation at Spotify, who has plans to tackle both these problems. Zonoozy left Spotify in 2023, and since then has set up his own music software label, A Vinyl Bar in Shibuya, a record label-meets-production studio that releases playful music apps the way labels drop records, including jetset.fm and Stacks . Essentially, it’s creating digital music playgrounds. While Shibuya’s products don’t have extensive libraries of music like typical streaming platforms, they offer users different ways to create new sounds, even if you only use them for a couple of minutes. But despite the label still being in its infancy, Zonoozy knows exactly where he wants to take it. I chatted with Zonoozy about where his post-Spotify career is heading, and his ambitious plans to insert his music services into a streaming world in which AI is becoming a growing presence. Music is participatory Bop is an interactive DJ music app that lets you mix and mess around with music (Image credit: A Vinyl Bar in Shibuya ) In a short period of time, Mauhan and his “small team of creative technologists” have released a slew of casual, interactive music platforms across web and mobile — but this is only the beginning. “I spent years at Spotify and I loved it,” Mauhan tells me. “Incredible company, incredible team. But I think I spent most of my time effectively thinking about what comes next. I started A Vinyl Bar in Shibuya around a simple belief that music is a verb, that the next major music platform should give people something to do with the music. It should be more participatory, more engaging”. Streaming has certainly made music a lot more accessible, but there was always one thing missing for Mauhan: interaction. “With streaming, you can hear almost anything, anywhere instantly, but the dominant interaction is still effectively sorting through folders and pressing play,” he continues. “There's an entire generation that was growing up playing with music through different mediums and different devices. I think their relationship with everything felt a lot more interactive.” This sparked a lightbulb moment for Mauhan, and his mission statement is simple: “to empower more people to express themselves with music, or feel self-expressive with music”. This is where his latest project, Bop, comes into play. (Image credit: A Vinyl Bar in Shibuya ) Bop is a pocket DJ app, currently in beta, that lets you mix, mash, and mess with music. Its interface is like an MPC workstation, allowing you to create remixes of popular songs by dragging and dropping effects and sounds onto its grid. “We're not all about replacing the creative process,” Mauhan adds. “We're more about building instruments and new ways to express yourself.” When it comes to the best music streaming services , tools like this aren’t a new concept — Spotify has its own DJ-style mixing feature — but Mauhan believes there’s still more room for music services whose focus is user expression. “I think there's a yearning for creative expression (in music platforms),” he says. “I think listening to music the way artists created and intended is absolutely a big part of it, but I also think having Legos that you play and interact with, engage with is also very important. “The next step in our journey is packaging that up into something that is platform scale, and we can actually deploy it and build a larger community of users and fans around it.” Next stop: a larger music platform In addition to Bop, borrowmyipod.com is a music service that lets you customize a classic iPod, and you can enter links for your Spotify and Apple Music playlists (Image credit: A Vinyl Bar in Shibuya) It’s clear that Zonoozy has had a blast developing Shibuya’s array of sonic playground tools, but what I want to know is if there’s a larger music platform on the horizon — and turns out, there is. “I think there's a bigger platform at the end of the tunnel for sure,” he tells me. “A Vinyl Bar in Shibuya is working actively on building it. I don't think it's gonna look or feel like any streaming platform you've seen before.” Now I’m intrigued — how will this platform compete with the likes of the music streaming big dogs? Turns out Zonoozy has thought about that too. “We believe it's going to be more participatory,” he shares. “We're not building something that puts the music in the background, we want to put it in the foreground”. And it's as simple as that. “The hints are in the products, and we want things that feel more playful and approachable. I don't think anyone's going to accuse us of building a DSP,” he adds. (Image credit: A Vinyl Bar in Shibuya ) Despite it still being in early stages of development, Zonoozy has a lot of faith in Shibuya’s bigger project; but music streaming tools are evolving rapidly as is tech in general, so he’s had to do a lot of thinking ahead. “My personal belief was that a lot of the cues around where media is going were in the gaming space,” he continues. “And I think interactive media was always a little bit ahead of the rest of the world in terms of film and music. I think because it was closer to technology, it was exploring the more creative technological boundaries of what you could do with media. “I think now with what's going on and how powerful these computers in our pockets are becoming, there's so much new, cool stuff you can do. It's a responsibility for all of us working in music and tech to figure out ways to do it that supports the industry, the community, and more than anything, the art form.” It occurs to me that Zonoozy is as interested in conserving as he is in innovating. Will music streaming survive without AI? (Image credit: A Vinyl Bar in Shibuya ) It wouldn’t be a discussion about where the music-streaming industry is going without me bringing up AI, and Zonoozy sounds dismissive about AI at first, telling me: “You know what I like about AI? It's easy to spell”. AI is having a big influence on music platforms in many ways, with algorithmic recommendations and tools such as AI playlist generators now pretty much part of the package. Because these features are right at users’ fingertips, I ask, will there come a time where listeners won’t be able to use services without the help of AI? Zonoozy has hope, saying, “It's hard for me to imagine a world where people are building things completely void of touching some semblance of AI, but I do believe that there will be products that are not purely driven by generative media.” While he doesn’t necessarily favor the reliance on AI tools to enhance the UX, Zonoozy isn’t against AI altogether. If anything, he acknowledges its benefits, and how it’s helped provide the foundations to his services. “It's enabling technology for us, it's just not the consumer proposition,” he adds. “Shibuya doesn't build LLMs or ask anyone to prompt music and wait for a finished song, but we do use it as a co-pilot for coding and development. I'd be naïve to say that there's no AI somewhere in the stack there. But on the music side, all the stems are all hand produced”. He continues, “I'm not anti-AI. I think AI is an incredible, powerful future-facing infrastructure. I think it can build so many cool things and empower so many cool things. I’m a traditionally strong techno optimist in that sense, I think it will lead to incredible discoveries and advancements — it makes coding infinitely easier. But AI is not our product thesis on our side.” When it comes to streaming services, there’s a huge focus on churning out tools designed to make the listening experience more personalized, more convenient, and more interactive. Given the pace of this evolution, I find it difficult to envisage where streaming culture is headed — Zonoozy shared my uncertainty. “In terms of streaming specifically, I don't know what's going to happen,” he admits. “The extreme levels of personalization to custom content made for you — I don't know where that line ends. Is it being personalised, or is it being generated for you?” ]]>

draft_context.source_title: Google pulling Nano Banana from Google Earth after one day shows how bad our AI misinformation problem has got
draft_context.description: We're now well past the point where it's very difficult, and in some cases impossible, to tell AI-generated photos and videos from the real thing. That means it's now important to treat everything you see online from untrusted sources with a big dose of skepticism. A newly rolled out Google Earth feature has apparently made AI-generated misinformation even more of a problem — and it highlights the scary potential of the technology, as well as the need for stronger guardrails to block the efforts of those who will instantly try and find the most subversive and harmful ways to use a new product. The feature is AI image generation in Google Earth, powered by the Nano Banana 2 model, and after a wave of inappropriate images were created and posted online, it's now been pulled while Google works on some more robust protections against misinformation. Google Earth's new feature Reimagining Pompeii was one way the feature could be used (Image credit: Google) It all started with the usual level of hype that Google builds around any new AI feature: the Nano Banana 2 image generation model that has already wowed us in the Gemini app would be available inside Google Earth on the web. "Generate custom images to help you visualize history, create real estate plans, and more," Google said . "For the first time, you can generate custom images using Google Earth's satellite, aerial, and 3D imagery alongside Nano Banana, which creates concepts grounded in the real world." Google had examples of how it could be used too: create an infographic about the Statue of Liberty, visualize your dream home by the lake, see what your neighborhood might look like a hundred years from now, or imagine Pompeii just before it got buried by ash and rock from an erupting Mount Vesuvius. All it took was a text prompt, and Google Earth would combine existing satellite and 3D data to create the AI image you were asking for. While the AI model wasn't new , adding it to the accurate and authentic imagery already in Google Earth was. What went wrong Infographics could be created with real-world information (Image credit: Google) Perhaps we should've seen this coming — and indeed some people did — but combining AI with the 3D data and satellite imagery of Google Earth didn't work out quite as well as Google hoped. The new upgrade was quickly used to create all manner of deceptive images that were then widely shared online. I'm reluctant to point you to them directly and give these fakes any more attention, but they're not hard to find on social media. Think natural disasters, terrorism attacks, giant sinkholes, alien activity, and refugee populations all in places where they never actually were, thanks to AI. Some of the images are clearly jokes, but many were produced deliberately to spread misinformation and confusion. That they were based on actual images sourced from Google Earth added extra credibility they wouldn't otherwise have had. And that was enough for Google to remove the feature. Google says a flood of images "that appear to violate our policies" mean that "we're rolling back this feature in Google Earth while we work on implementing stronger guardrails". The company added:."It's important to note that generated images didn't appear in the main Google Earth experience for others to see and were watermarked as AI generated." Our AI-filled future Google Earth-based visions of the future will have to wait (Image credit: Google) You don't have to look for long online to find rather strong anti-AI sentiment building up among users, especially when it comes to image and video content. The general sentiment on Reddit is that there's "zero use" to a feature like this, and that users are fed up with AI being "shoved down our throats" . There are various obvious lessons to be learned here: firstly not everything needs to have an AI prompt box or an AI element to it, and if some tools are largely AI-free, that's fine. Microsoft recently rolled back some of the AI it added to Notepad — an app where a big part of the appeal is its simplicity — after user complaints. Secondly, before companies release any new AI features, they need to consider the worst-case scenarios in terms of how they're going to be used. The internet as a collective is going to immediately try and stress test them in the most deceptive and unwholesome ways, and there need to be safety measures put in place around that. Lastly, it's never been more important to stick to sources of information that you know you can trust: not random social media accounts, but established publications that have policies around AI and its use. That's one effective way you can tell the difference between what's trustworthy and what isn't. ]]>

A newly rolled out Google Earth feature has apparently made AI-generated misinformation even more of a problem — and it highlights the scary potential of the technology, as well as the need for stronger guardrails to block the efforts of those who will instantly try and find the most subversive and harmful ways to use a new product.

The feature is AI image generation in Google Earth, powered by the Nano Banana 2 model, and after a wave of inappropriate images were created and posted online, it's now been pulled while Google works on some more robust protections against misinformation.

It all started with the usual level of hype that Google builds around any new AI feature: the Nano Banana 2 image generation model that has already wowed us in the Gemini app would be available inside Google Earth on the web.

Trong Đề án Cải cách tổng thể thị trường tài chính Việt Na m, chính phủ nhắc đến việc nghiên cứu, đánh giá khả năng triển khai đồng tiền kỹ thuật số quốc gia (CBDC) . Quyết định này gây chú ý lớn trong cộng đồng vì đây là xu hướng mới, đang được nhiều quốc gia nghiên cứu, thí điểm. Tín hiệu từ Thanh Nien Cong Nghe cần được đặt vào bối cảnh trước: thời điểm xuất hiện, chi tiết đã có cơ sở và lý do nó đáng nằm trong dòng tin công nghệ hôm nay. Phần này cần dựng lại thay đổi đã có cơ sở trước khi chuyển sang nhận định.

sections.heading: Tác động thực tế với người đọc
sections.body: Theo World Bank (Ngân hàng Thế giới), CBDC là tiền do ngân hàng trung ương phát hành, được tạo ra và ghi nhận dưới dạng số trên sổ cái tập trung hoặc phi tập trung, được định danh bằng đơn vị tiền tệ hiện hành. CBDC có thể chuyển đổi thành tiền mặt, tiền gửi ngân hàng thương mại và các hình thức tiền tệ khác theo yêu cầu của người nắm giữ tại các tổ chức được ủy quyền. Phần này cần nối câu chuyện với workflow, chi phí, bảo mật hoặc quyết định dùng/mua của người đọc.

sections.heading: Chi tiết cần kiểm chứng
sections.body: Về vai trò pháp lý, CBDC là phương tiện thanh toán hợp pháp (legal tender), tương tự tiền pháp định. Câu hỏi tiếp theo là tín hiệu này có thành rollout bền vững, thay đổi giá trị sản phẩm, giới hạn đáng chú ý hay chỉ là một nhịp cập nhật ngắn. Phần này chỉ giữ chi tiết có thể kiểm chứng và tránh lặp lại nguyên văn cách diễn đạt của nguồn.

sections.heading: Ai nên hành động hoặc chờ
sections.body: Về quy mô ảnh hưởng, CBDC sẽ tác động đến kinh tế vĩ mô, chính sách tiền tệ. Nó cung cấp một phương tiện lưu trữ giá trị an toàn và phương thức thanh toán hiệu quả, có thể làm tăng cạnh tranh trong việc huy động vốn tiền gửi, tăng thị phần của các ngân hàng trong nguồn vốn bán buôn và giảm lợi nhuận của ngân hàng. Với người đọc, khung hữu ích gồm bằng chứng hiện có, nhóm bị ảnh hưởng, rủi ro còn lại và điểm nên kiểm tra trước khi hành động. Phần này cần gọi đúng nhóm độc giả nên hành động ngay hoặc nên chờ thêm xác nhận.

sections.heading: Điều cần theo dõi tiếp
sections.body: Trong khi CBDC được phát hành bởi ngân hàng trung ương và được đảm bảo tính pháp định, Bitcoin và stablecoin (tiền ổn định neo giá 1:1 theo USD hoặc tài sản như vàng) lại được tạo ra bởi các cá nhân hoặc tổ chức, dựa trên mạng lưới phi tập trung. Một bài tốt cần tách rõ sự kiện từ nguồn, tác động với người đọc và câu hỏi theo dõi để không giống bản tóm tắt link rời. Phần này nên khép lại bằng tín hiệu cần kiểm tra tiếp, không tóm tắt lại cùng một ý.

sections.heading: Tác động thực tế với người đọc

Nguyên nhân xuất phát từ việc các tiến trình chạy ngầm chiếm dụng bộ nhớ cao hơn nhiều so với phiên bản trước. Mọi tác vụ từ khởi chạy ứng dụng đến mở File Explorer đều bị ảnh hưởng và giật lag. Phần này cần nối câu chuyện với workflow, chi phí, bảo mật hoặc quyết định dùng/mua của người đọc.

sections.heading: Chi tiết cần kiểm chứng
sections.body: Windows 11 đi kèm quá nhiều phần mềm rác cài sẵn gây tốn tài nguyên hơn hẳn Linux hay macOS. Không chỉ Microsoft, các nhà sản xuất linh kiện cũng cài thêm vô số tiện ích bên thứ ba không cần thiết. Những chương trình này chiếm dụng bộ nhớ và tiêu tốn tài nguyên hệ thống chạy ngầm nghiêm trọng. Phần này chỉ giữ chi tiết có thể kiểm chứng và tránh lặp lại nguyên văn cách diễn đạt của nguồn.

sections.heading: Ai nên hành động hoặc chờ
sections.body: Bên cạnh đó, toàn bộ giao diện người dùng cũng bị đánh giá là quá cồng kềnh và thiếu tối ưu. Menu tìm kiếm chứa nhiều ô không cần thiết, trong khi chức năng tìm kiếm lại thường xuyên bị lỗi. Việc thiếu đi trải nghiệm sạch sẽ ngay từ đầu đã khiến người dùng quay lưng với hệ điều hành . Với người đọc, khung hữu ích gồm bằng chứng hiện có, nhóm bị ảnh hưởng, rủi ro còn lại và điểm nên kiểm tra trước khi hành động. Phần này cần gọi đúng nhóm độc giả nên hành động ngay hoặc nên chờ thêm xác nhận.

sections.heading: Điều cần theo dõi tiếp
sections.body: Cập nhật vốn được coi là yếu tố thiết yếu để cải thiện bảo mật và độ ổn định hệ thống. Tuy nhiên trên Windows 11, các bản cập nhật lại liên tục phát sinh lỗi nghiêm trọng sau khi cài đặt. Số lượng bản cập nhật lỗi gia tăng trong năm nay khiến sự thất vọng của công chúng đạt đỉnh điểm. Một bài tốt cần tách rõ sự kiện từ nguồn, tác động với người đọc và câu hỏi theo dõi để không giống bản tóm tắt link rời. Phần này nên khép lại bằng tín hiệu cần kiểm tra tiếp, không tóm tắt lại cùng một ý.

Để cộng đồng nhanh chóng tiếp cận những nội dung quan trọng, AlphaTest 01 chuẩn bị sẵn nhiều hỗ trợ: Nhận ngay cấp 125, Mở đầy đủ kỹ năng, miễn phí reset điểm, Trang bị xanh full option, Hỗ trợ thêm trang bị, nguyên liệu và thú cưỡi, Tự do chuyển đổi môn phái, Trải nghiệm PK, săn Boss và các hoạt động nổi bật khác,....

Những hỗ trợ trên giúp người chơi chủ động kiểm tra nhiều môn phái, kỹ năng và cách xây dựng nhân vật mà không cần mất thời gian phát triển lại từ đầu. Các phản hồi trong AlphaTest 01 sẽ được ghi nhận làm cơ sở để Tepaylink tiếp tục tối ưu sản phẩm trước khi chính thức ra mắt.
Võ Lâm Tình Kiếm 3D hỗ trợ nhiều nền tảng gồm PC Client, Android APK, giả lập và iOS qua TestFlight, đáp ứng thói quen trải nghiệm khác nhau của cộng đồng game thủ.
